cards.text: Pregnancy-shame micro-angle (MOT-A-002.1, sourced, HIGH). One-to-one replication of the Arctic Goddess fogged-mirror static: finger-drawn torso doodles + arrow, hand-printed mirror copy, hand holding the bottle bottom right. Skeleton kept verbatim: IF [recognition beat], THIS IS FOR YOU. Three hook variations, one shared art direction. Engine: one GPT Image 2 prompt per ad at quality high, Motilli product passed as reference image, 3:4 padded to 4:5. Deviation from reference: doodle labels read BACKED UP... -> MOVING! instead of Before.../After!, because Meta prohibits before-and-after weight-loss imagery and Motilli claims regularity, not fat loss.

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: AD 1 PRIMARY TEXT
cards.text:
Flat at eight in the morning. By two in the afternoon the button is undone and you are holding your bag in front of you.

Fat does not arrive on that schedule. A stomach that changes shape between breakfast and lunch is holding what should already have moved through.

Your colon is a muscle, and it only contracts when it gets a signal. That signal is a short-chain fatty acid called butyrate, made by the bacteria in your colon when fiber reaches them. Once transit slows, less material reaches those bacteria, fewer of them survive, and less butyrate gets made. Weaker signal, slower colon, and even less gets down there tomorrow. The loop tightens a little every week it is left alone.

Laxatives force one movement and rebuild nothing. Coarse fiber dropped onto a colony that has already been starved down just sits there and distends you worse by evening.

Motilli does both halves at once. Concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of apigenin, which barely absorbs into the bloodstream and so stays down in the colon where the work is. Plus a fine soluble fiber that feeds the butyrate makers specifically, without the bulk that bloats.

Three gummies before bed with a full glass of water. It is not a laxative, so the first few days are quiet. The first normal, non-cramping movement usually lands around day five and fills in from there.

If you are on a GLP-1, the same loop runs harder, and rebuilding the gut does not touch the weight loss. Those are two separate systems.

Ninety days to decide. Email inside ninety days and every dollar comes back, no return required.

cards.title: AD 2 PRIMARY TEXT
cards.text:
You know the move. Someone lifts a phone and before you have decided anything, your hand is flat across your middle and your elbow is pulled in.

That is not vanity. You are managing a stomach that invites a question you should not have to answer, and hiding it is easier than explaining it.

What is underneath it is mechanical. The colon is a muscle and it needs a signal to contract. That signal is a short-chain fatty acid called butyrate, and you do not make it yourself. The bacteria in your colon make it out of the fiber that reaches them. When things slow down, less reaches them, the colony thins out, butyrate drops, and the colon moves slower still. What stays behind ferments, and fermenting stool is what pushes the wall of your abdomen out by the afternoon.

That is also why the drawer has not worked. Probiotics drop fresh bacteria into an environment that cannot hold them. More fiber feeds a colony that is no longer there.

Motilli rebuilds the environment and then feeds what grows back, in one gummy. Concentrated celery juice standardized for apigenin, which stays down in the colon instead of absorbing into the blood, and a fine soluble prebiotic fiber for the butyrate makers.

Three before bed. Third-party tested, lab results posted. Ninety days to try it and every dollar comes back if the afternoons stay the same.

cards.title: AD 3 PRIMARY TEXT
cards.text:
The jeans fit this morning. They came off around five, something loose went on instead, and nobody at the table knew that happened.

The usual suspect is dinner. The thing actually taking up the room is what dinner turned into three days ago and never left.

Here is the mechanical version. Your colon contracts on a signal called butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid that the bacteria in your colon produce out of the fiber that reaches them. Slow the transit down and less reaches them. The colony shrinks, butyrate falls, the muscle gets a weaker signal, and less gets through the next day. It feeds on itself, which is why this gets worse over the years instead of settling.

Stool sitting in a colon that is not moving keeps fermenting, and gas has to go somewhere. That is the afternoon.

Motilli works on the cause rather than forcing an exit. Concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of apigenin, which barely absorbs into the bloodstream and therefore stays where the problem is, plus a fine soluble fiber that feeds the butyrate makers so they can signal again.

Three gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Not a laxative, nothing is forced.

Ninety days, money back, no return required. A rebuild takes weeks, so the guarantee outlasts the timeline.

cards.title: PRODUCT TRUTH
cards.text:
Relief routes through regularity only, meaning less retained fermenting stool. No standalone de-bloat ingredient claim. No chlorophyll.

Dose: three gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Not a laxative.

DELIBERATELY ABSENT: the 'when are you due' stranger beat. The angle record flags it as dramatised and not in the corpus. All three hooks are self-identification, never testimony.

cards.title: AUDIT
cards.text:
Six-month shelf life: PASS. Nothing seasonal or transitional.

Swap test: PASS. Copy argues against laxatives, fiber powders and probiotics by mechanism. The apigenin-stays-in-the-colon detail and the rebuild-then-feed order are ours.

Law 2: PASS. No invented study, percentage, doctor, review count or customer quote.

Law 9: PASS. No em dashes, no negation-affirmation beats, no parallel stacks, no rhetorical openers.

VERIFY BEFORE LAUNCH: the 90-day no-return-required guarantee wording against the live policy page.
